note: Arm 3a for #47. Nine of the twenty `refinement` corpus entries refer to a canvas the transcript never shows. The other ten paste their history inline and need nothing. `chat-refine-nothing-to-refine` is excluded on purpose: #55 describes it as 'a refinement turn arriving with no previous diagram', so giving it one destroys the case. It stays as the control that must still refuse.
expectationsChange: Supplying history changes the right answer. Four of these are `outcome: no-diagram` in #55 because, with nothing on the canvas, refusing is correct. With a diagram supplied, editing it is correct. `expectedType` and `expectedOutcome` here OVERRIDE the corpus for this arm only, and every override is stated below with its reason.

refine-2-add-a-branch.code:
flowchart TD
    Signup[User signs up] --> Send[Send verification email]
    Send --> Click[User clicks link]
    Click --> Verified[Account verified]
refine-2-add-a-branch.why: Turn 2 of the refine-N chain. The branch to add is the expiry path off Click.

refine-3-change-a-shape.code:
flowchart TD
    Signup[User signs up] --> Send[Send verification email]
    Send --> Click[User clicks link]
    Click --> Verified[Account verified]
    Click --> Expired[Link expired]
    Expired --> Send
refine-3-change-a-shape.why: Turn 3, so the canvas is turn 2's output. 'The third box' is Click, which needs four boxes present to be resolvable at all.

refine-5-change-type.code:
flowchart TD
    Signup[User signs up] --> Send[Send verification email]
    Send --> Click{Link still valid?}
    Click -->|yes| Verified[Account verified]
    Click -->|no| Expired[Link expired]
    Expired --> Send
refine-5-change-type.why: THE sticking test. Four turns of flowchart on the canvas and seven words throwing the type away. If passing history makes the model stick, it shows here first.

chat-refine-direction.code:
flowchart TD
    Ingest[Ingest] --> Validate[Validate]
    Validate --> Transform[Transform]
    Transform --> Load[Load]
chat-refine-direction.why: OVERRIDE: #55 says no-diagram because 'same diagram, just make it left to right' is unanswerable with no diagram. With one, redrawing it LR is the whole job.

chat-refine-spoken.code:
flowchart TD
    DB[(Postgres)] --> AuthSvc[Auth Service]
    DB --> BillingSvc[Billing Service]
chat-refine-spoken.why: The arrows point the wrong way and the database is on top, which is what 'no not like that' is objecting to.

chat-refine-vague-improve.code:
flowchart TD
    A[start] --> B[thing happens]
    B --> C[other thing]
    A --> C
    C --> D[done]
    B --> D
chat-refine-vague-improve.why: OVERRIDE: #55 says no-diagram because 'make it cleaner' names nothing. With a diagram present and genuinely untidy labels plus crossing edges, redrawing it is answerable.

chat-refine-deictic-chain.code:
flowchart TD
    Queue[Queue] --> Worker[Worker]
    Worker --> Store[Store]
chat-refine-deictic-chain.why: OVERRIDE, and the weakest of the four. #55 notes mermaid cannot express position, so 'move that one under this one' stays undeliverable even with perfect history. 'Connect it to the last one' is deliverable, so a redraw with one added edge is the pass. If this one fails it is not evidence against passing history.

class-refine-add-method.why: Order must already exist for 'add a cancel() method to Order' to be an edit rather than a new diagram.
